newsitem.title: USA: Maine to ask voters to approve $40 mln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Maine to ask voters to approve $40 mln of bonds.

text.p: Maine is planning to ask its voters to approve or reject a total of around $40 million of bond initiatives on the state ballot when they head to the polls on November 5, the state deputy treasurer said on Wednesday.
If the bond acts are approved by the voters, Gov. Angus King then would have 90 days to ratify them.

While ratification by the governor would allow the various departments to begin planning the projects that would be financed by the debt, Maine does not plan to sell any of these bonds for around one year, said Maurice Stickney, deputy treasurer. He added the offering probably would be sold through negotiation.
The following are highlights of the initiatives, which would raise money for four projects.
--$16.5 million to clean up public health, hazardous substance discharge sites, including tire stockpiles, with $9 million set aside for drinking water grants for cities and towns.
--$11 million to encourage job growth and economic vitality by helping agricultural enterprises and small businesses get capital.
--$10 million to clean up water pollution and drinking water problems.
--$3 million for capital improvements at state parks.
